rationale: This LXX verse number carries the Ephraim census heading rather than the MT Zebulun line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: διαρρησσων διαρρηξω την βασιλειαν σου εκ χειρος σου και δωσω αυτην τω δουλω σου
chosen_rendering: And the Lord said to Solomon, Because these things came to be with you and you did not keep my commandments and my ordinances that I commanded you, in tearing I will tear your kingdom out of your hand and give it to your servant.
alternate_renderings: I will surely rend your kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
rationale: Greek doubles the tearing verb here. Current wording keeps that emphatic pattern visible.

greek_phrase: ζησεσθε και πολλοι εσεσθε και ευλογησει σε κυριος ο θεος σου
chosen_rendering: If you obey the commands of the Lord your God that I command you today, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his ordinances and his judgments, then you shall live and be many, and the Lord your God will bless you in all the land into which you are entering there to inherit it.

rationale: Greek says live and be many rather than live and multiply. Current wording keeps that line.

greek_phrase: ουκ εκτοκιεις τω αδελφω σου τοκον αργυριου και τοκον βρωματων και τοκον παντος πραγματος ου αν εκδανεισης

rationale: This LXX verse number carries the no-interest-to-brother line rather than the MT foreigner line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και εδωκαν οι υιοι ισραηλ τοις λευιταις τας πολεις και τα περισπορια αυτων
chosen_rendering: And the sons of Israel gave to the Levites the cities and their surrounding lands.
alternate_renderings: Aaron and his sons offered on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the Levite-city grant line rather than the MT Aaronic service line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: ο ανηρ αυτης στησει αυτη και ο ανηρ αυτης περιελει
chosen_rendering: Every vow and every binding oath to afflict a life, her husband shall establish it for her, and her husband shall remove it.
alternate_renderings: Her husband shall confirm it, or her husband shall cancel it.
rationale: Greek uses the establish-remove pair here. Current wording keeps that direct legal phrasing.

greek_phrase: ανατελει αστρον εξ ιακωβ και αναστησεται ανθρωπος εξ ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: I will point him out, but not now. I count him blessed, and he is not near. A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a man shall stand up out of Israel, and he shall crush the leaders of Moab and plunder all the sons of Seth.
alternate_renderings: A star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel.
rationale: Greek says a man shall stand up out of Israel rather than a scepter shall rise. Current wording keeps the Greek figure.

greek_phrase: και αποστειλον μοι ξυλα κεδρινα και αρκευθινα και πευκινα εκ του λιβανου
chosen_rendering: And send me cedar woods and juniper woods and pine woods from Lebanon, because I know your servants know how to cut woods from Lebanon, and behold, your servants are with my servants,

rationale: This LXX verse number carries the timber request line rather than the MT artisan request line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και ιησους και βαναιας και σαραβια ησαν συνετιζοντες τον λαον εις τον νομον και ο λαος εν τη στασει αυτου
chosen_rendering: And Iesous and Banaias and Sarabia were causing the people to understand the law, and the people stood in their place.
alternate_renderings: Jeshua and Bani and Sherebiah and many others caused the people to understand the law.
rationale: Greek here gives a shorter personnel list and ends with the people standing in their place. Current wording keeps that form.

greek_phrase: εν ταις ορασεσιν ιωηλ του ορωντος περι ιεροβοαμ υιου ναβατ
chosen_rendering: And rest of matters of Salomon, first and last, behold, written in words of Nathan prophet and in words of Achia the Sēlōnite and in visions of Iōēl the seer concerning Ieroboam son of Nabat.
alternate_renderings: In the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.
rationale: Greek names Iōēl here rather than the familiar MT Iddo. Current wording keeps the Greek source list.

greek_phrase: ουχ ουτως η κλινη εφ' ης ανεβης εκει ου καταβηση απ' αυτης οτι θανατω αποθανη
chosen_rendering: And Elijah spoke to him and said, Thus says the Lord: Why is it that you sent messengers to seek in Baal of flies, god of Akkarōn? And not so, the bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die.

greek_phrase: και ουκ εξεθλιψαν οι υιοι δαν τον αμορραιον τον θλιβοντα αυτους εν τω ορει
chosen_rendering: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their clans, their cities and their villages. alternate_renderings: The border of the children of Dan went out too little for them; therefore the children of Dan went up against Leshem.

greek_phrase: και της φωνης αυτου ακουσεσθε και αυτω προστεθησεσθε
chosen_rendering: After the Lord your God you shall walk, and him you shall fear, and his commands you shall keep, and his voice you shall hear, and to him you shall be joined.

rationale: Greek ends with to him you shall be joined. Current wording keeps that form rather than smoothing to cling.

greek_phrase: ανθ' ων υψωσα σε απο της γης και εδωκα σε ηγουμενον επι τον λαον μου ισραηλ

rationale: Greek says from the earth here and ends with vanities. Current wording keeps those details.

greek_phrase: ος αν δω του σπερματος αυτου αρχοντι θανατω θανατουσθω
chosen_rendering: And to the sons of Israel you shall say: If any of the sons of Israel or of the newcomer newcomers in Israel gives of his seed to a ruler, he shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
alternate_renderings: Whoever gives any of his seed to Molech shall surely be put to death.
rationale: Greek says to a ruler here rather than naming Molech. Current wording keeps the transmitted Greek wording.

greek_phrase: εκαλεσαν νηστειαν και εκαθισαν τον ναβουθαι εν αρχη του λαου
chosen_rendering: They proclaimed a fast and seated Nabouthai at the head of the people.
alternate_renderings: It happened when Ben-hadad heard this message while drinking that he said, Set yourselves in array.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the Nabouthai fast line rather than the MT Ben-hadad war line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: εν τοπω ου εαν ακουσητε την φωνην της κερατινης εκει συναχθησεσθε προς ημας και ο θεος ημων πολεμησει περι ημων

greek_phrase: ουτος εποιησεν τω θυσιαστηριω παραθεμα εργον δικτυωτον κατωθεν του πυρειου υπο αυτο εως του ημισους αυτου
chosen_rendering: He made for the altar a surrounding frame of net-work beneath its fire-pan underneath it as far as its middle, and he fixed to it four bronze rings on the four sides of the frame of the altar, wide enough for the bars, so that the altar might be carried by them.
alternate_renderings: All the gold used for the work in all the work of the sanctuary was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the altar-network construction line rather than the MT gold totals line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: εαν δε ολιγοστοι ωσιν οι εν τη οικια ωστε μη ικανους ειναι εις προβατον
chosen_rendering: But if those in the house are too few for an animal from the flock, he shall take along his neighbor nearest to him according to the number of persons. Each according to what is enough for him shall be counted toward the animal from the flock.
alternate_renderings: If the household is too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbor next to his house take it.
rationale: Greek says animal from the flock here rather than lamb alone. Current wording keeps that broader term.

greek_phrase: δανιεις εθνεσιν πολλοις συ δε ου δανιη και αρξεις συ εθνων πολλων σου δε ουκ αρξουσιν
chosen_rendering: May the Lord open for you his good treasury, the heaven, to give rain to your land in its season and bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow, and you shall rule many nations, but they shall not rule you.
alternate_renderings: You shall lend to many nations and you shall not borrow.
rationale: Greek adds the rule-many-nations line here. Current wording keeps the fuller blessing promise.

greek_phrase: πλην εν τω καιρω του γηρως αυτου επονεσεν τους ποδας αυτου
chosen_rendering: And the rest of the matters of Asa and all his dominion that he exercised, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Iouda? Yet in the time of his old age his feet were in pain.
alternate_renderings: In the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
rationale: Greek says his feet were in pain here. Current wording keeps that simpler expression.

greek_phrase: και αφανιεις τον πονηρον εξ υμων αυτων
chosen_rendering: And that prophet or that dreamer of the dream shall die, because he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt, who redeemed you from slavery, to drive you out of the way that the Lord your God commanded you to walk in it. alternate_renderings: So you shall put the evil away from your midst.
rationale: Greek says destroy the evil one from among you. Current wording keeps the singular personified form.

greek_phrase: λεπρα εμμονος εστιν η αφη ακαθαρτος εστιν
chosen_rendering: And the priest shall inspect the mark on the seventh day. If the mark has spread in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in the leather, in whatever is made of leather for use, the mark is persistent skin-disease. It is unclean.

rationale: Greek says persistent skin-disease here. Current wording keeps that direct expression.

greek_phrase: εν τη εορτη η επλασατο απο καρδιας αυτου
chosen_rendering: And he went up upon the altar that he made on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the feast that he devised from his own heart, and he made a feast for the sons of Israel and went up upon the altar to offer incense.
alternate_renderings: In the feast which he had devised of his own heart.
rationale: Greek says devised from his own heart. Current wording keeps that sharper line.

greek_phrase: και συνεφωνησαν οι ιερεις του μη λαβειν αργυριον παρα του λαου και του μη ενισχυσαι το βεδεκ του οικου

rationale: This LXX verse number carries the priestly agreement line rather than the MT collection order. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: μη ελθωσιν οι απεριτμητοι ουτοι και εμπαιξωσιν μοι

rationale: Greek says mock me here. Current wording keeps that verb.

greek_phrase: τους αποφθεγγομενους εν κινυραις και εν ναβλαις και εν κυμβαλοις
chosen_rendering: And king Dauid and rulers of force appointed for works sons of Asaph and Haiman and Idithon, those prophesying with lyres and harps and cymbals, and their number by head was according to their works.

greek_phrase: πατριαρχαι αρααβ καθως οι αδελφοι αυτου οι νεωτεροι
chosen_rendering: And they too received lots, like their brothers sons of Aaron, before king and Sadok and Achimelech and chiefs of father-houses of priests and Levites, elder fathers like their younger brothers.

rationale: Greek keeps the elder-fathers versus younger-brothers contrast here. Current wording leaves that contrast visible.

greek_phrase: εζεκιαν τον ηγουμενον του λαου μου
chosen_rendering: Turn back and say to Ezekias the leader of my people, Thus says the Lord God of Dauid your father: I heard your prayer, I saw your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you will go up into the house of the Lord.

rationale: Greek says leader of my people here. Current wording keeps that term.

greek_phrase: ουτος ο νομος της ολοκαυτωσεως αυτη η ολοκαυτωσις επι της καυσεως αυτης επι του θυσιαστηριου ολην την νυκτα εως το πρωι
chosen_rendering: Charge Aaron and his sons, saying, This is the law of the whole burnt offering: this is the whole burnt offering on its burning upon the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall burn on it; it shall not be extinguished.

greek_phrase: και δωσω τα κωλα σου και τα κωλα παρεμβολης αλλοφυλων εν ταυτη τη ημερα τοις πετεινοις του ουρανου
chosen_rendering: And the Lord will shut you up into my hand today, and I will kill you and remove your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners in this day to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
alternate_renderings: I will give the carcasses of the army of the Philistines this day to the birds of the sky.
rationale: Greek says limbs and limbs of the camp here. Current wording keeps that concrete body-part wording.

greek_phrase: αυχενα επιστρεψουσιν εναντι των εχθρων αυτων οτι εγενηθησαν αναθεμα
chosen_rendering: The sons of Israel will certainly not be able to stand against the face of their enemies. They will turn neck before their enemies, because they have become a devoted thing. I will not add to be with you any longer unless you remove the devoted thing from among you.
alternate_renderings: They will turn their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed.
rationale: Greek says turn neck and become a devoted thing here. Current wording keeps those harder forms.

greek_phrase: οτι εχθραινουσιν αυτοι υμιν εν δολιοτητι οσα δολιουσιν υμας δια φογωρ και δια χασβι
chosen_rendering: because they act as enemies toward you in the deceit with which they deceive you over Peor and over Chasbi daughter of the chief of Midian, their sister, the one struck down on the day of the plague over Peor.
alternate_renderings: Because they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.
rationale: Greek doubles the deceit language and keeps the Chasbi form. Current wording preserves that texture.

greek_phrase: και τοδε το δικαιωμα αυτου πασας τας ημερας ας εκαθητο δαυιδ εν αγρω των αλλοφυλων
chosen_rendering: And he did not keep alive man and woman to bring into Geth, saying, Lest they report in Geth against us, saying, Thus David does. And this was his rule all the days David sat in the countryside of the foreigners.
alternate_renderings: This was his manner all the while he dwelt in the country of the Philistines.
rationale: Greek says this was his rule and sat in the countryside of the foreigners. Current wording keeps that form.

greek_phrase: ου δυνηση υπεριδειν
chosen_rendering: Thus you shall do with his donkey, and thus you shall do with his garment, and thus you shall do with every loss of your brother, whatever may be lost from him and you find. You shall not be able to overlook it.
alternate_renderings: You may not hide yourself.
rationale: Greek says you shall not be able to overlook it. Current wording keeps that direct expression.

greek_phrase: γεγονεν μεθ' ημων ημερας τουτο δευτερον ετος και ουχ ευρηκα εν αυτω ουθεν
chosen_rendering: And the satraps of the foreigners said, Who are these passing over? alternate_renderings: Has he not been with me these days or these years? and I have found no fault in him.
rationale: Greek says these days, this second year and I found nothing in him. Current wording keeps those details.

greek_phrase: και ουκ ηβουληθην αποκτειναι σε και εφεισαμην σου
chosen_rendering: Behold, on this day your eyes have seen that the Lord delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and I was not willing to kill you, and I spared you and said, I will not put my hand upon my lord, because he is anointed of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: I would not slay thee, but spared thee.
rationale: Greek says I was not willing to kill you and I spared you. Current wording keeps both verbs.

greek_phrase: και ελαβον τον επισιτισμον του λαου εν τη χειρι αυτων και τας κερατινας αυτων
chosen_rendering: And they took the food of the people in their hands and their horns, and he sent every man of Israel away, each to his tent, but the three hundred men he kept. And the camp of Midian was beneath him in the valley.
alternate_renderings: They took the provision of the people in their hand and their trumpets.
rationale: Greek says food of the people in their hands and keeps the three hundred men he kept line. Current wording preserves that scene.

greek_phrase: ει αληθως πασιν υμιν δωσει ο υιος ιεσσαι αγρους και αμπελωνας και παντας υμας ταξει εκατονταρχους και χιλιαρχους
chosen_rendering: And Saoul said to his servants standing by him, Hear now, sons of Benjamin. Will the son of Iessai truly give to all of you fields and vineyards and appoint all of you centurions and commanders of thousands,

rationale: Greek says centurions and commanders of thousands here. Current wording keeps those military titles.

greek_phrase: εξεκκλησιασεν την συναγωγην ιουδα και σκηπτρον βενιαμιν εκατον και εικοσι χιλιαδες νεανιων
chosen_rendering: And Roboam entered Ierousalem and assembled the congregation of Iouda and the scepter of Benjamin, one hundred twenty thousand young men who make war, to fight against the house of Israel, to return the kingdom to Roboam son of Solomon.

rationale: Greek says scepter of Benjamin and one hundred twenty thousand young men here. Current wording keeps those Greek details.

greek_phrase: και εβασιλευσατε τον αβιμελεχ υιον της παιδισκης αυτου επι τους ανδρας σικιμων
chosen_rendering: but you rose up against my father's house today and killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and made Abimelech, son of his maidservant, king over the men of Sikima because he is your brother,

rationale: Greek says maidservant and Sikima here. Current wording keeps those forms.

greek_phrase: ουκ εγνωσαν το κριμα του θεου της γης και απεστειλεν εις αυτους τους λεοντας
chosen_rendering: And they said to the king of the Assyrians, The nations whom you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria did not know the judgment of the god of the land, and he sent the lions among them, and behold, they are putting them to death because they do not know the judgment of the god of the land.

greek_phrase: φθεγξασθε φωνην ανακρουομενων ανα μεσον ευφραινομενων

greek_phrase: και ενεγκαι τα πρωτογενηματα της γης ημων και πρωτογενηματα καρπου παντος ξυλου
chosen_rendering: and to bring firstfruits of our land and firstfruits of fruit of every tree, year by year, into house of the Lord,

greek_phrase: επεβλεψας επι το θυμιαμα μου και εις την θυσιαν μου αναιδει οφθαλμω
chosen_rendering: And why did you look upon my incense and upon my sacrifice with shameless eye, and glorify your sons beyond me, to bless yourselves from the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before me?

greek_phrase: διηλθον δια της γης σελχα και διηλθον δια της γης εασακεμ και ουκ ην και διηλθον δια της γης ιακιμ
chosen_rendering: And they passed through the hill-country of Ephraim, and they passed through the land of Selcha and did not find them, and they passed through the land of Easakem and it was not there, and they passed through the land of Iakim and did not find them.
alternate_renderings: They passed through the land of Shalisha and the land of Shalim and the land of the Benjamites.
rationale: Greek gives the place forms Selcha, Easakem, and Iakim here. Current wording keeps those forms.

greek_phrase: και τα αγαθα των ποιμνιων και των βουκολιων και των εδεσματων και των αμπελωνων και παντων των αγαθων
chosen_rendering: And Saoul and all the people preserved Agag alive and the good things of the flocks and the herds and the foods and the vineyards and all the good things, and they were not willing to destroy them. But every dishonored and worthless thing they destroyed.

greek_phrase: ενα αιροντα τρια αιγιδια και ενα αιροντα τρια αγγεια αρτων και ενα αιροντα ασκον οινου
chosen_rendering: And you will pass on from there and beyond, and you will come as far as the oak of Thabor, and you will find there three men going up to God at Baithēl, one carrying three kids, one carrying three vessels of breads, and one carrying a skin of wine.

greek_phrase: απεστρεψαν το προσωπον απο της σκηνης κυριου και εδωκαν αυχενα
chosen_rendering: Because our fathers rebelled and did evil before Lord and forsook him and turned face away from tent of Lord and gave neck.

rationale: Greek says gave neck here rather than turned backs. Current wording keeps that image.

greek_phrase: εξελθη το παιδιον αυτης μη εξεικονισμενον επιζημιον ζημιωθησεται καθοτι αν επιβαλη ο ανηρ της γυναικος δωσει μετα αξιωματος
chosen_rendering: If two men fight and strike a pregnant woman, and her child comes out not yet formed, he shall pay a penalty according as the woman's husband lays upon him. He shall pay with assessment.

rationale: Greek says child comes out not yet formed and pay with assessment. Current wording keeps those juridical details.

chosen_rendering: And house which I am building is great, because our God is great above all gods.
alternate_renderings: Behold I build a house to the name of the Lord my God to dedicate it to him and to burn before him sweet incense...

greek_phrase: τους ανδρας τους ασεβεις τους εν γαβαα τους υιους βελιαλ και θανατωσομεν αυτους και εξαρουμεν κακιαν εξ ισραηλ
